deities: Shiva (Swayambhu linga in Ardhanarishwara form, kept covered with a metal bowl)

history.summary: Medieval Shiva temple atop Madanchala (Madanchalla) Hill in Hajo, one of the town's Pancha Tirtha. The central chamber holds a rare Swayambhu (self-originated) Shiva linga in the Ardhanarishwara (androgynous) form, normally kept hidden under a metal bowl. Inscriptions record that the temple and its two adjacent walls were built by Ahom King Rajeswar Singha in 1753. ASI surveyor Spooner's 1912 field survey observed stone molding of a different character from an older temple beneath and recorded the alternate name 'Kedarnatha temple' - so 1753 is better read as a rebuilding than a first foundation. Two sacred ponds adjoin the complex, and a stone stair through the forest leads to a large rock-cut image of Ganesha. Date conflict flagged: one heritage source attributes the temple's initiation to Koch king Naranarayan in the 16th century - needs verification against the Ahom-period inscriptions.

name: Kedareswar Temple (Kedar Temple)
town_description: Hajo is an ancient pilgrimage town about 30 km west of Guwahati, revered by Hindus, Buddhists and Muslims alike - the Hayagriva Madhava temple, the Powa Mecca dargah and several old Shiva shrines make it one of Assam's Pancha Tirthas (five sacred sites). The town blends Koch, Ahom and Pala-era heritage and is a major day-trip destination from Guwahati.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati (~35-40 km) is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Guwahati Railway Station (~32 km) is the nearest major railway station.
travel.road: About 32 km from Guwahati with daily bus services; a stone stair climbs through forest to the hilltop shrine.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the month of Sawan (July-August) is especially significant for Shiva worship.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published online - verify locally before visiting.
